text:
Situation: Sufentanil citrate has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2022-05-03 and remains current as of 2026-10-21, a span of 54 months. Corvale East holds 64 units (7.1 days), Corvale General holds 134.07 units (16.1 days), and Corvale Lakeside holds 50 units (21.4 days). The rule‑ranked option is to transfer 17 units from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East, raising East to 9 days on hand while Lakeside retains two weeks.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2022-05-03 and it is still listed as current on 2026-10-21. The product used at Corvale East and Corvale General carries NDC 00409338221 labeled by Hospira, Inc., and SPL set ID 20293943 identifies the same labeler and plant. FDA inspection 1110899 at that plant ended 2019-11-21 and was classified VAI, with the classification letter dated 2020-02-12 — 894 days before the shortage posting. Earlier inspections at the same plant include OAI classifications on 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, and 2011-08-04, and a Warning Letter on 2010-04-12. The most recent inspection on record ended 2025-02-07 and was classified NAI.

Our position: Inventory at Corvale East is critically low. Corvale Lakeside has sufficient supply to support a transfer without dropping below two weeks on hand. Corvale General also has adequate stock but Lakeside is the preferred source per the ranked options.

Recommended actions:
1. Approve transfer of 17 units from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
2. If Lakeside transfer cannot be executed, approve transfer of 17 units from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
3. Monitor daily usage at all three sites and report updated days‑on‑hand to the P&T committee weekly — requires pharmacy director and P&T chair concurrence.
4. Continue tracking FDA shortage status for any change in supply outlook — requires pharmacy buyer to update the committee at each meeting.

Not recommended: Initiate any clinical protocol changes, dose substitutions, or alternative agent selections; those decisions rest with treating clinicians and the committee.
